topics.topic: How authored file fixtures and their digest metadata enter add_trial_case
questions: For authored cases with file input or expected-output ports, what does the operation receive so it can persist the fixture bytes: the bytes themselves, an existing file reference, or only digest/size/media-type facts?
For a file port in an authored trial case, does the request carry the fixture bytes, an existing StoredValue reference, or only file facts, and who computes and publishes its content digest?
How do authored file-fixture bytes enter add_trial_case, and who computes and verifies their digest and size?

judgement.why: This is the same authored file-fixture representation and byte-publication question judged in P1, and the reopening change did not alter the relevant passages.

precedent.topic: Authored file-fixture representation and responsibility for computing and publishing its metadata and bytes
quotes: A contract version, input values by port, optional expected outputs, the actor.

The producing attempt — `run_id`, node, `map_index`, `attempt_number` — the
port and `list_index`, the file's bytes and its port's media type.

Complete and digest-checked before it is visible; `spool_file_bytes_max` per
file and `spool_run_bytes_max` per run (A15 rule 3).
precedent.why: The change did not touch the authored-trial payload or spool-file contracts and did not make their byte and digest handling newly consequential.

topics.topic: Required input and expected-output port coverage in authored trial cases
questions: When expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every output port, or may it assert only a subset of outputs?
Must authored inputs contain exactly every contract input and no extra names, and, when expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every contract output or may it specify a subset?
Must an authored trial case supply exactly the contract’s input ports, with no additional names?
When expected outputs are present, must they cover exactly all contract output ports, or may they assert only a subset?

judgement.why: This is the same authored trial-case port-coverage question judged in P2, and the reopening change did not alter the relevant passages.

precedent.topic: Required and permitted authored trial-case input and expected-output port keys
quotes:
### Inputs

A contract version, input values by port, optional expected outputs, the actor.

### Enforces

Fit in port name order — presence, carriage, schema, size; inputs take the
port's class, expected outputs the highest class of the inputs (A04 rule 1,
M21).
precedent.why: These passages were unchanged by the reopening change, which only renamed store changes and refined persistence-module ownership.

topics.topic: Unit used for disclosed classified failure-detail length
questions: What unit is used for the disclosed length: UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another measure?
Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, or characters after replacement and truncation?

quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
judgement.why: The later notes specify that the disclosed length is the UTF-8 byte length.

topics.topic: Capabilities and A08 rule 5 checks performed by check_installed_instances
questions: Without a particular operation or proposed ports, which A08 rule 5 checks are applied to a service record at startup, whether unrelated capabilities are validated, and in what order multiple failing capabilities are considered?
Which capabilities, if any, are validated during check_installed_instances, and which subset of A08 rule 5 counts as a record-level check here?

quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST take the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raise RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
judgement.why: The later notes limit startup validation to read_service_record's record-level checks and the specified credential-header collision checks, with explicit service and check ordering.

topics.topic: Context and identity profiles used for content digests and list sorting
questions: How does the operation know which identity profile and list-sorting rules to apply, especially for plain JSON values, manifest capability entries, request descriptions and model records with lists?

How does the operation distinguish a model identity, a JSON value digest, an idempotency-key digest and a request digest so that model-specific list sorting is applied only where intended, and how is a raw file's content_digest computed?

quotes: content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For every content variant of IdentitySubject (contract_version, implementation, trial_case, flow_version, stored_value, corpus) MUST build one JSON object whose members are exactly the variant's fields keyed by field name, subject_kind included, with nested models as objects keyed by field name, tuples as arrays, enum members as their value text, None as null and JSON-text fields such as value_schema kept as JSON strings, take its canonical bytes with canonical_bytes and return the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of those bytes.

content_identity: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Before hashing, lists whose order carries no meaning MUST be sorted so that the same content in another order has the same identity: ports by (direction, name), flow nodes by node_id, flow edges by (to_node, to_port, from_node, from_port), flow constants by (to_node, to_port), all compared as text by Unicode code point; every other list keeps its order, in particular trial_case_ids of a corpus (corpus order is meaningful) and the elements of any JSON value.

content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the idempotency_key variant MUST build one JSON object with one member per entry of fields, named by the entry's port and holding the JSON value its canonical_json encodes, so the order of the fields does not change the key, and return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of its canonical bytes; a field whose value is null is kept as null, not dropped.

content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the json_text variant MUST return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of json_text, and for the bytes variant the hexadecimal SHA-256 of content exactly as given, without any canonicalization; this is the digest of a file and of a value's bytes.

prepare_request: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] request_digest is content_identity of the canonical JSON of the description, so equal requests give equal digests, a rotated credential value changes nothing and any other difference changes the digest; the credential value never appears in the description, the digest or any reason.
judgement.why: The later contracts define distinct content-identity variants, their sorting rules, request-description hashing, and raw-byte hashing for files.

topics.topic: Errors and precedence for missing references when capturing a trial case
questions: If the named contract version is missing and the source run also no longer holds its spool, which error must be returned first?
What error is returned when the named contract version, executed implementation or referenced SpooledFile does not exist?

judgement.why: This is the same missing-reference classification question for captured trial cases judged in P5, and the reopening change did not alter the relevant passages.

precedent.topic: Error classification for missing references in captured trial cases
quotes:
A missing record is `unknown_reference`
  naming it, whatever operation looked it up.

### Errors

`refused` naming the first failing check.
precedent.why: The missing-reference and captured-case error passages were unchanged, and the persistence refactor did not make their classification newly consequential.

topics.topic: How retries, attempts, and approvals determine an operation element's current conclusion
questions: Which attempt and approval records determine the current conclusion when an element has several NodeExecutions, EffectAttempts and approved or requested approvals after resumption or a not_applied resolution?
Which attempt determines the element’s current conclusion, and how are earlier waiting or unknown attempts combined with later attempts?

quotes: operation_element_conclusion: [BEHAVIOR] MUST trust the run, pinned version and element its caller passes and check none of them; it reads the element's NodeExecutions through read_records with ExecutionsOfElement, its EffectAttempts with AttemptsOfElement and its approvals with ApprovalsOfElement, and the binding's output ports through read_flow_version of the run's flow_version_id and read_binding of the node's binding_id; the trace is its only source.

operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt resolved not_applied waits with reason owner_approval and no approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; with no NodeExecution and no requested approval the element is not reached.

operation_element_conclusion: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns one ElementConclusion variant: ElementSucceeded with output PortRefs, ElementFailed with status and detail_code, ElementWaiting with reason (= models.WaitReason) and approval_id only for owner_approval, or ElementNotReached; a failed read propagates as an internal error and nothing is refused.
judgement.why: The later notes select the highest-attempt-number NodeExecution and give the complete precedence for its associated attempt and requested approval.
